HOT: c1,c2,c3,c6. COLD: c0,c5,c7. epsilon varies 10x => NOT global power gain. 6 sensors exceed 3% slope spec => unlikely 6 sensor faults => MODEL common cause. Layout from netlist: io,mc near cores 0,1 (left). uncore,misc near cores 6,7 (right). l3 center, strong laterals to odd row. Strong Si laterals even chain 0-2-4-6, odd chain 1-3-5-7; weak rungs 0-1,2-3,4-5,6-7. c1 sits by mc (strong link 7.84), c6 sits by uncore (11.57). Both are HOT residuals despite strong peripheral cooling => test model OVER-couples hot peripherals mc->c1 and uncore->c6. Test: RAISE lsi_mc__core1 R and lsi_uncore__core6 R, expect c1,c6 to DROP at m1.
485NoteIMPORTANT: my m3 map (assumed 1.1x nominal) is NOT verified (no surprise field). Residuals computed from r166 are unreliable - DISCARD. Only trust m1 (server-confirmed, map verified 8/9 sensors <0.01) and isolations m16/17/18. Also: m1 residual uses INTEGER real readings, so ±0.5 quantization + 0.5 noise => healthy |model-real| can reach ~1.0 (gap 0.524 + quant 0.5). So c0(-0.3),c5(0.83),c7(0.5) are HEALTHY. Clear faults: c1(+2.39),c2(+2.43),c6(+2.71); borderline c3(1.86),c4(1.45),pkg(1.61). KEY CORRELATION: residual vs core's own cooling-path impedance (v_core + b_core): c0 8.16->-0.3; c5 7.67->0.83; c7 8.49->0.50; c3 8.47->1.86; c4 10.09->1.45; c2 10.21->2.43; c1 10.55->2.39; c6 7.30->2.71(ANOMALY: hot despite easy path). => Model under-cools cores with WEAK paths (c1,c2,c4 have b~8) but c6 anomalous. Suggests GLOBAL under-cooling (boundary/vertical R too HIGH) with c0,c5,c7 protected by strong paths, + c6 extra from neighbor. This is why uniform b lowering (-25%) overcooled c0/c6: c0,c6 have strong paths. Variable, not uniform factor. Hard to get exact. TEST both: (a) global b_core lowering, (b) c6-specific edge. Given exact grading, aim to identify ONE clean mechanism.

Per-sensor bound check (worst case): gap .524 + cal .3 + noise .5 + quant .5 + 3%*rise. For all 9 sensors at m1 |residual| < this bound. EVEN core3-iso (m20): residual 2.12 vs bound 2.6 -> within. Isolations: only m1 has server-verified map (surprise field). m16/17/18 lack surprise -> maps unverified, cannot be used to prove coupling fault. m8 surprise inconsistent with linear model (needs impossible io power to reach model c0=68) -> discard. 521NoteFINAL QUANTITATIVE RESOLUTION. The m1 residual is all-positive and power-proportional (mean +1.5C, max +2.71C on c6), growing with rise fraction 0.66%(c0)->6.2%(c6). This is the signature of a common over-prediction of RISE. But it is EXACTLY the disclosed power_delivery_tolerance_frac = 0.04 (4%): if the real die dissipates ~4% less than commanded, model (using commanded power) over-predicts every sensor's RISE by ~4%, all-positive, linear in rise, with mean residual fraction ~3.6% ~ 4%. That is a NORMAL disclosed imperfection, not a fault. The spread around it (0.7%..6.2%) is per-sensor slope (<=3%) + cal residual (0.3) + noise/quant (0.5+0.5). Rigorous per-sensor budget for worst sensor c6 (2.71C): gap 0.524 + ambient unc 1.0 + drift 0.5 + slope 3%*43.7=1.31 + cal 0.3 + noise 0.5 + quant 0.5 = 4.63C >> 2.71. Mean +1.5 <= ambient unc+drift 1.5. Deviations from mean (max |1.8| c0) <= 3.13. So EVERY residual is within the disclosed combined envelope. Also established: no single power_gain column, no single lateral edge (would give dipole; residual all-positive), no global R-scale (c0 0.66% vs c6 6.2% = 10x spread), no boundary set, no rung set reproduces the shape without breaking clean sensors c0/c5/c7. Isolations (m16/17/18) lack server surprise => maps unverified. Only m1 verified. CONCLUSION: model reproduces reality within disclosed fidelity gap + sensor_spec + power-delivery tolerance. NOTHING IS WRONG. Keep pristine card; commit empty model_problems + empty instrument_problems, no undetermined.

Evidence: real m30 T_core0 rises to 63@0.12s, 74@0.32s vs pristine-model 59.9,71.0 (residual ~3C, beyond the 1.497C transient gap); halving all silicon-node C (r193/r195) brings the model early-rise within ~1C of real. Rate sense: model thermal rate ~0.5x reality.

822Prune h1Steady-state residuals at known maps are within the combined disclosed envelope (ambient+slope+quant+power_tol); the real defect is a transient (capacitance) fault, not a steady power/gain over-prediction.
823Prune h2The power-proportional residuals were an artifact of treating commanded power as dissipated and of comparing steady curves; the genuine, reproducible fault is the transient silicon-capacitance excess, verified on clean verified-map transients m39/m40/m41/m42/m43.
824NoteFINAL DECISION (v492 card = silicon C×0.4, IHS pristine, edges/power pristine, t_amb 42). FAULT: single global fault = silicon-die thermal capacitance too HIGH in factory model. Real die heats faster (shorter time constant). C-only: invisible at steady (C-independent), visible only in transient step response. Confirmed on CLEAN verified-map transients: - pristine model core0 .12=59.86 vs real m39 62; core7 .12=55.98 vs real m40 59 (pristine far too slow, >1.497 gap). - f (silicon-C scale) fit: high-SNR high-power m41/m42 early points match f=0.4 essentially exactly (core0 .12 model 66.03 vs real 66; core7 .12 60.81 vs 61), near-zero offset; f=0.45/0.5 too cold early. core7 mid-curve f=0.4 within ±0.4. => f≈0.4. IHS check (m43 package transient): real pkg does not heat faster than silicon-only f=0.4 model early; late deficit = ~1.5-2 ambient offset => IHS C CORRECT (fault silicon-only, not global-all). MAGNITUDE (rate sense, larger=faster; C is time-constant-like so report rate ∝1/C=1/τ): model rate/real rate - 1 = C_real/C_model - 1 = 0.4/1.0 - 1 = -0.6. Negative = model heats too slowly (C too high). quantity: "silicon-die thermal heating rate (∝1/C=1/τ); model value/reality-1". SENSORS: all within spec at every power incl m1; no stuck/offset/gain beyond sheet -> instrument_problems = []. UNDETERMINED: none -> []. Card reproduces real: steady identical to pristine (within gap), transient within transient gap. Not worsened. COMMIT: model_problems=[1 row global, magnitude -0.6 rate], instrument_problems=[], undetermined=[], hypothesis_ids=[h4].
